Programs

Duke Energy Florida - Smart $aver Commercial Energy Efficiency Rebate Program

Last Updated February 20, 2025

Program Overview

  • Implementing Sector:
    Utility
  • Category:
    Financial Incentive
  • State:
    Florida
  • Incentive Type:
    Rebate Program
  • Web Site:
    https://www.duke-energy.com/business/products/smartsaver
  • Administrator:
    Small/Medium Business Customer Service
  • Utilities:
    Progress Energy Florida Inc
  • Eligible Efficiency Technologies:
    Chillers, Heat pumps, Air conditioners, Heat recovery, Energy Mgmt. Systems/Building Controls, Duct/Air sealing, Building Insulation, Other EE
  • Applicable Sectors:
    Commercial
  • Incentive Amount:
    Building Envelope Improvements
    Ceiling Insulation Upgrade (available for retrofit projects only): $0.17/sq. ft.
    Wall Insulation (available for retrofit projects only): $0.10/sq. ft.

    HVAC Equipment
    High-Efficiency Chillers: $20 per ton
    Large Unitary AC Units and Heat Pumps >65,000 Btu/h: $50 per ton
    Packaged Terminal Heat Pumps and Air Conditioners (available for retrofit projects only): $67 per ton
    Small Heat Pumps <65,000 Btu/h (available for retrofit projects only): $50 per ton

    HVAC-Related Improvements
    Demand Control Ventilation (DCV): $50 per ton
    Duct Check Program (available for retrofit projects only): See program brochure
    High-Efficiency Energy Recovery Ventilation (ERV): $.75 per CFM

    Business Energy Check
    Get a Free Energy Assessment, See website for details

    Custom Incentive Program
    Air-Cooled Chiller Maintenance Tune-up: Not Specified, contact Duke Energy
    Thermal Energy Storage: up to $300 per kilowatt (kW) of reduced cooling at peak times.
  • Equipment Requirements:
    See program website for information on equipment requirements

Summary

Duke Energy Florida offers incentives to its business customers for replacing their old equipment with high-efficiency models, and for making improvements to their existing equipment. Interested customers should refer to the program website and related brochures for more details including incentive levels and equipment requirements.

About DSIRE®

DSIRE is the most comprehensive source of information on incentives and policies that support renewables and energy efficiency in the United States. Established in 1995, DSIRE is operated by the N.C. Clean Energy Technology Center at N.C. State University and receives support from EnergySage.
